newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nouvelles Frontieres head to bid for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: Nouvelles Frontieres head to bid for Air Liberte.

text.p: The head of French travel company Nouvelles Frontieres said on Thursday he was planning to bid for both troubled Air Liberte and airline AOM, paving the way for a possible "French solution" to the carriers' ownership.
"It is certain I will bid for AOM...I will also undoubtedly put in an offer for Air Liberte," Nouvelles Frontieres president Jacques Maillot told Reuters.
The Paris daily Le Monde reported this week that French Prime Minister Alain Juppe had told the Finance Ministry to back a "national solution" to Air Liberte's troubles.
But Maillot said he was not acting at the government's behest. "I am not at the beck and call of the government," he said.
Maillot said he had just received the files on troubled Air Liberte, placed under bankruptcy protection by a Paris court on September 26, and was studying them.
Bids for Air Liberte are due by October 14.
Maillot said there was no rush to buy AOM, held by state agency Consortium de Realisation (CDR) which groups the assets of state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais slated to be sold off.

British Airways, which has a foothold in France through its French carrier TAT, has expressed an interest in buying Air Liberte, merging it with TAT and investing the money needed to make the entity viable.

Last week, it asked Europe's Transport and Competition commissioners to block any bid by AOM to acquire Air Liberte, saying it would be an illegal use of state aid. CDR was created as part of a state bailout of Credit Lyonnais.
Maillot said in an interview that buying AOM and Air Liberte would allow Nouvelles Frontieres "to achieve more rapid external growth...there are lots of synergies."
Alexandre Courvelaire, the president of French carrier AOM is also reported to be studying making an offer for Air Liberte, by forming a bidding group.
Before Air Liberte was placed under credit protection, its chairman Lofti Belhassine was in merger talks with AOM chairman Courvelaire but the two could not find common ground.

French domestic airlines such as AOM, Air Liberte and Air France's Air Inter - renamed Air France Europe -- are engaged in a bitter price war following liberalisation of some key routes in France ahead of a full opening up of the market.
